stories.headline: Nvidia tells customers AI server prices will rise more than 15% as memory costs soar

key_facts.fact: Nvidia notified some of its largest customers on Saturday, August 22, that prices of servers containing its AI chips will rise by more than 15% in many cases.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has told some of its largest customers that the prices of servers containing its AI chips will rise by more than 15% in many cases, Bloomberg reported on Saturday.

key_facts.fact: The increases take effect on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems shipping in early 2027, with the size of each hike depending on chip generation and memory configuration.
key_facts.excerpt: The increases will take effect on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems shipping early next year... The size of each increase will depend on the chip generation and the memory configuration involved.

key_facts.fact: Contract makers building servers for Microsoft, Google and Oracle have already passed word of the increases to their customers; some server makers have told customers Nvidia system prices could rise about 17%.
key_facts.excerpt: Some server makers have told customers that prices for Nvidia's major AI server systems could rise by about 17 percent, according to U.S. technology publication The Information.

key_facts.fact: Server DRAM contract prices jumped 53-58% in the second quarter of 2026 and are forecast to rise another 13-18% in the third quarter, according to TrendForce.
key_facts.excerpt: Contract prices for server DRAM jumped 53 to 58 percent in the second quarter of this year from the previous quarter. They are expected to rise another 13 to 18 percent in the third quarter, according to market researcher TrendForce.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia runs a gross margin of roughly 75%, so the hikes signal it intends to pass memory cost inflation to customers rather than absorb it.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia runs a gross margin of roughly 75% non-GAAP, among the highest in the semiconductor industry, and the reported hikes indicate the company intends to pass memory cost inflation on to customers rather than absorb it.

key_facts.fact: TrendForce says Nvidia is considering diversifying the HBM setup of its upcoming Rubin Ultra chip, adding 8-stack HBM4E and HBM4 options to the originally planned 12-stack HBM4E, expecting the DRAM shortage to run through 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: According to TrendForce, Nvidia is considering diversifying the HBM configuration of its upcoming Rubin Ultra chip — adding 8-stack HBM4E and HBM4 options alongside the originally planned 12-stack HBM4E — in anticipation that the DRAM shortage could extend through 2027.

stories.headline: XPeng's humanoid robot unit raises over $900M at a $6.3B valuation, a China record

key_facts.fact: XPeng announced on August 24, 2026 that its robotics business signed share purchase agreements raising over US$900 million at a post-money valuation above US$6.3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: XPENG (NYSE: XPEV) announced that its robotics business has signed share purchase agreements with multiple global investors to raise over US$900 million, implying a post-money valuation of over US$6.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by IDG Capital with Gaorong Ventures participating and Tencent and Alibaba as strategic investors; XPeng calls it the largest single-round private financing in China's embodied AI industry.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Xpeng said on Monday its robotics business raised over $900 million in its first funding round, led by IDG and Gaorong Ventures and with Tencent and Alibaba as strategic investors.

key_facts.fact: This is the robotics unit's first external funding round; XPeng will keep controlling ownership and continue to consolidate it into the group's financial statements.
key_facts.excerpt: It is the robotics unit's first external funding round... XPENG will retain controlling ownership of the robotics business when the deal closes, and the unit will remain consolidated in the group's financial statements.

key_facts.fact: The valuation centers on IRON, XPeng's next-generation humanoid, which has 76 degrees of freedom in the body and 21 in each hand and runs on three Turing AI chips delivering up to 2,250 TOPS of on-device compute.
key_facts.excerpt: IRON carries 76 degrees of freedom across its body and 21 in each hand, runs on three Turing AI chips delivering up to 2,250 TOPS of on-device compute, and executes tasks autonomously without remote operation.

key_facts.fact: IRON is targeted for mass production by end-2026, with initial deployment in XPeng stores and campuses and deliveries in China and abroad from 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: XPENG IRON is expected to enter mass production by the end of 2026, with initial commercial deployment at XPENG's stores and campuses, before officially launching and beginning deliveries in China and overseas markets in 2027.

key_facts.fact: The unit's previous round was a Series A of more than $100 million in July 2022, also led by IDG Capital, when its product was a quadruped robotic pony.
key_facts.excerpt: In July 2022, the unit then known as XPENG Robotics closed a Series A of more than $100 million, also led by IDG Capital... at the time the largest single round in China's bionic robotics sector in two years, and the unit's product was a quadruped robotic pony aimed at households.

stories.headline: Xiaomi launches Xring O3, a 3nm phone chip, plus its first 3nm self-driving processor

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi unveiled the Xring O3 on August 24 at a chip technology conference in China, alongside two other in-house chips, the Xring D100 and Xring O100.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the Chinese manufacturer Xiaomi has officially introduced its Xiaomi Xring tri-chip solution in its home country, China, which includes Xiaomi Xring O3, Xiaomi Xring D100 and Xiaomi Xring O100.

key_facts.fact: The O3 is built on TSMC's 3nm process, packs more than 24 billion transistors (26% more than its predecessor) and has a 133mm² die.
key_facts.excerpt: It runs on TSMC's 3nm process technology and has more than 24 billion transistors – a 26% increase compared to the XRING O2 chip... It further has a die size of 133mm².

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi says the O3 is the world's first mobile chip to support LPDDR6 memory, reaching 10,667Mbps and 113.8GB/s of bandwidth, 48% more than the Xring O1.
key_facts.excerpt: the 3nm chip is the world's first mobile processor to support LPDDR6, delivering speeds of up to 10,667Mbps and memory bandwidth of 113.8GB/s, a 48% increase over the XRING O1.

key_facts.fact: The chip scored 5,228,014 on AnTuTu and uses a deca-core all-big-core CPU whose multi-core score tops 15,000 for the first time, a 60% gain.
key_facts.excerpt: The Xiaomi Xring O3 is a flagship AI SoC. It has achieved an AnTuTu score of 5.22 million. The CPU features a deca-core design with all large cores, achieving a multi-core score exceeding 15,000 for the first time, representing a 60% performance improvement.

key_facts.fact: The Xring D100 is billed as China's first 3nm high-performance AI chip for autonomous driving, with a 20-core CPU, a 16-core NPU, support for up to 160GB of unified memory and local deployment of models up to 200B parameters.
key_facts.excerpt: The Xiaomi Xring D100 is China's first 3nm high-performance AI chip for intelligent driving. It utilises an advanced 3nm process and features a powerful combination of a 20-core high-performance CPU and a 16-core high-performance NPU. It supports up to 160GB of unified memory and can locally deploy ultra-large models with up to 200B parameters.

key_facts.fact: The Xiaomi 18 Fold will be the first device with the Xring O3, followed by the Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max; both launch in China next month.
key_facts.excerpt: Xiaomi has officially announced that the Xiaomi 18 Fold will be the first to feature the Xring O3 AI flagship processor, while the Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max will also be equipped with this chipset. Both devices will be launching next month in China.

stories.headline: Humanoid robots beat Usain Bolt's 100m record at Beijing's World Humanoid Robot Games

key_facts.fact: On the opening day of the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday, August 22, a humanoid robot ran the 100m in 9.39 seconds, beating Usain Bolt's human world record of 9.58 seconds.
key_facts.excerpt: A humanoid robot has broken the human record in the 100-meter dash by completing the sprint in just 9.39 seconds, surpassing Jamaican legend Usain Bolt's world record of 9.58 seconds, at a preliminary race at the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games (WHRG) on Saturday evening at Beijing's 'Ice Ribbon' stadium.

key_facts.fact: Two hours later another robot lowered the mark to 9.32 seconds.
key_facts.excerpt: A humanoid robot clocked 9.39 seconds to beat the men's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds during the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games preliminary events in Beijing on Saturday. Only two hours later, another robot refreshed the record with 9.32 seconds.

key_facts.fact: The 9.39s run was by Tiangong Ultra, built by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Centre; Honor's robot Lightning also beat Bolt with 9.47s, while Unitree Robotics' entry finished last at 12.41s.
key_facts.excerpt: Tiangong Ultra clocked 9.39 seconds in a preliminary heat, beating the men's world record of 9.58 seconds held by Jamaican sprinting great Usain Bolt since 2009. Another robot in the heat, Lightning, also finished faster than Bolt in a time of 9.47 seconds... Unitree Robotics' robot was not as quick, finishing last with a time of 12.41 seconds.

key_facts.fact: At last year's inaugural games the winning 100m time was 21.50 seconds — meaning robot sprint times were cut by more than half in one year.
key_facts.excerpt: The results mark a sharp improvement from last year's inaugural event, when Tiangong Ultra won over the same distance in 21.50 seconds

key_facts.fact: The games are held at the National Speed Skating Oval built for the 2022 Winter Olympics, and opened the same week as Beijing's 2026 World Robot Conference, where roughly 3,000 products were shown.
key_facts.excerpt: The games, which are taking place in the National Speed Skating Oval built for the 2022 Winter Olympics, opened the same week as Beijing held the 2026 World Robot Conference, where companies showcased around 3,000 products, including humanoid robots.

stories.headline: Abbott says data centers 'dug their own grave' as Trump calls opposition a mistake

key_facts.fact: On ABC's 'This Week' on Sunday, August 23, Texas Governor Greg Abbott said data center companies 'basically dug their own grave for the problem that's been caused for them. And that's why they got the backlash they deserve.'
key_facts.excerpt: Abbott told Karl on ABC's 'This Week' that the backlash stems partly from the sheer speed of the buildout... 'They basically dug their own grave for the problem that's been caused for them,' he continued. 'And that's why they got the backlash they deserve.'

key_facts.fact: Abbott said Texas has paused approvals for new data centers while statewide standards are put in place, and that future projects must meet requirements on water use, electricity demand, consumer costs and local community approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Abbott said, who added that Texas has paused approvals for new data centers while new statewide standards are implemented. Abbott said future projects in Texas will have to meet requirements related to water usage, electricity demand, consumer costs and local community approval before they can move forward.

key_facts.fact: Abbott called Texas the 'epicenter of AI development' last November when he joined Google to announce a $40 billion investment in three data center campuses.
key_facts.excerpt: Just last November, Abbott called Texas the 'epicenter of AI development' as he joined Google to announce a $40 billion investment into three data center campuses.

key_facts.fact: 61% of Americans now oppose building a new data center in their area, up from 49% in March, according to an Annenberg Public Policy Center survey; opposition runs 69% among Democrats, 54% Republicans and 53% independents.
key_facts.excerpt: 61% of Americans now oppose construction of a new data center in their area, according to an Annenberg Public Policy Center survey last month, up from 49% in March. The opposition crosses party lines: 69% of Democrats, 54% of Republicans and 53% of independents oppose new data centers in their area.

key_facts.fact: In an interview with Michael Cohen that aired in full on Sunday, President Trump said communities that oppose data centers are 'making a mistake' because they create tremendous amounts of jobs and money.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump says communities that oppose data centers are 'making a mistake' as they create 'tremendous amounts of jobs and money', amid bipartisan backlash. President Trump defended the expansion of data centers in an interview with his former fixer, Michael Cohen, that aired in full on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Abbott said last week that fewer than 10% of data center companies had responded to a state request for information needed to project future power demand; ERCOT is tracking a more than 500% increase in peak electricity demand.
key_facts.excerpt: He said Texas law requires data centers to report their power and water usage, but fewer than 10 percent were in compliance... 'Many are unaware that ERCOT is tracking a more than 500 percent increase in peak electricity demand.'

key_facts.fact: New York became the first state to enact a statewide moratorium on large new data centers; Delaware, Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia have active efforts to restrict or pause development.
key_facts.excerpt: states with active or recent efforts to restrict, pause or temporarily ban data center development include Delaware, Georgia, Michigan, New York, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia... The most significant action came in New York, which became the first state to enact a statewide moratorium on large new data centers.

stories.headline: At Hot Chips, Samsung bets on custom HBM while SK hynix bets on hybrid bonding

key_facts.fact: At Hot Chips 2026, held August 23-25 at Stanford University, Samsung and SK hynix laid out competing approaches to the memory bottleneck in AI computing.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, the two leaders of the global high-bandwidth memory (HBM) market, laid out competing approaches to easing memory bottlenecks before an audience of researchers from around the world.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's Han Sang-wook presented custom HBM (cHBM), which tailors the base die at the bottom of an HBM stack to each customer's GPU or NPU — for example Nvidia's and AMD's — strengthening only the functions they need.
key_facts.excerpt: The design tailors the base die to the graphics processing units (GPUs) and neural processing units (NPUs) used by customers such as Nvidia and AMD, strengthening only the functions they need, such as speed or power efficiency.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix America vice president Lee Jae-sik said hybrid bonding can narrow TSV circuits and widen the core die by 24%, and that the company is researching whether to apply it to seventh-generation HBM4E.
key_facts.excerpt: Lee explained that hybrid bonding can narrow TSV circuits compared with existing methods and widen the core die, which makes up most of an HBM, by 24%... 'We don't know yet whether it will be applied to HBM4E, the seventh generation, but we are researching hybrid bonding techniques.'

key_facts.fact: SK hynix is spending about 19 trillion won on the P&T7 advanced packaging plant in Cheongju and building an HBM packaging and R&D base in Indiana.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix is investing approximately 19 trillion won in Cheongju to construct P&T7, an advanced packaging production facility, while also establishing an advanced packaging production and R&D base for HBM in Indiana, U.S.

key_facts.fact: SK hynix also published a co-packaged optics roadmap in Nature Electronics with global researchers, integrating optical transceivers with processors in a single package.
key_facts.excerpt: On this day, SK hynix unveiled a Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) technology roadmap in the international academic journal Nature Electronics alongside global researchers, integrating optical transceivers with processors in a single package.

key_facts.fact: This year's Hot Chips opened with a tutorial on memory technology — last year's opening tutorial was on data center racks — a sign the AI infrastructure race is shifting toward memory bottlenecks.
key_facts.excerpt: A notable feature of this year's event is that the first official tutorial will focus on memory technology. Last year, the opening tutorial was on data center racks. This year's choice underscores how the center of gravity in the AI infrastructure race is shifting toward easing memory bottlenecks that supply data.
